Lift Chair — SmartTek® LED Diagnostics

All Models
💡 SmartTek LED Locations

Three green LED lights illuminate when power is present. If any light is out, an electrical fault exists at that point.

1
Hand Control
On hand control body
2
Transformer
On transformer body
3
Motor Wire
Wire from motor to transformer
AutoDrive Note: AutoDrive hand controls have a "Lights Out" feature — backlight dims after ~15 sec inactivity. Press any button to wake before diagnosing.
🔍 Step-by-Step Diagnosis
Step 1 — Verify Power
Chair plugged in? Outlet has power? Check circuit breaker.
Step 2 — Check All Connections
Confirm outlet wire is tight into transformer. Motor wire plugged firmly into transformer.
Step 3 — Read the LEDs
Motor wire LED out, transformer LED on: Power not reaching motor or control box.
Hand control not lit, transformer & motor wire on: Defective hand control or extension wire.
All LEDs on but chair won't move: Check lockout feature or perform calibration.
⚙️ Unlock & Calibration Procedures
If all LEDs are on but the chair won't move or positions feel off, use these procedures. AutoDrive hand controls only.
Lockout Unlock: Hold M button until backlight flashes → press and release Rise/Up button.

5-Zone Calibration

  • Footrest/backrest won't fully extend
  • Positioning seems off
  • General periodic maintenance
While standing beside the chair, press and hold the highlighted buttons simultaneously (LUMBAR + footrest arrows) until the chair stops moving, then hold an additional 5 seconds.

4-Zone Calibration

  • Footrest/backrest won't fully extend
  • Positioning seems off
  • General periodic maintenance
While standing beside the chair, press and hold the highlighted buttons simultaneously (HEAD + footrest arrows) until chair stops moving, then hold an additional 5 seconds.

Scooter — Controller Beep Codes

Buzzaround XL GB117 / GB147
🔊 Beep Code Quick Reference

The controller beeps a repeating count when a fault is detected. Count the beeps, find the code below, and follow the resolution steps.

Code Fault Severity Cause & Resolution
#1 Battery Low Warning Battery voltage low — scooter may drive slowly. Recharge immediately.
#2 Battery Very Low Stop Scooter will not operate. Recharge or load test batteries. Replace if they won't hold charge.
#3 High Battery Voltage Warning Battery voltage above 26VDC. Allow level to drop. Verify charger is approved Golden charger.
#4 Current Limit Timeout Warning Motor exceeded max current too long. Turn off, cool 10 min. May indicate faulty motor, poor batteries, excessive weight, or uphill overuse.
#5 Brake Fault Stop Park brake release switch active or brake faulty. Disengage/re-engage park brake. If persists, test brake resistance (should be 45–52 ohms). Replace motor/brake assembly if out of range.
#6 Paddle Fault — Out of Neutral Warning Throttle paddle not in neutral when key turned on. Check for obstruction. Ensure paddle springs back to center. If recurring, test throttle pot (proceed to Code #7).
#7 Throttle/Speed Pot Fault Stop Fault with throttle pot, speed pot, or wiring. Test resistance across throttle pot pins 1-3 (expected 5k ohm ±10%). Replace throttle pot or main harness as indicated.
#8 Motor Voltage Fault Stop Internal motor problem. Test motor resistance (0.8–1.5 ohms). Test brake resistance (45–52 ohms). Replace motor/brake assembly if out of range. Replace controller if in range.
#9 Controller Fault Stop Internal controller fault. Remove key, allow to cool. If code persists, replace controller.
Before any troubleshooting: Reset circuit breaker · Check for terminal corrosion · Confirm battery terminals secure · Ensure batteries fully charged · Verify all electrical connections seated properly.

Power Wheelchair — No Power Checklist

All Models
⚡ Power Wheelchair No-Power Diagnosis
1. Check Circuit Breaker
Reset breaker on battery box. Resistance across breaker should be less than 10 ohms.
2. Check Battery Charge
Batteries should read 12–14VDC each when fully charged. Load test if draining quickly.
3. Check Freewheel Lever
Ensure freewheel lever is in the fully engaged (drive) position before powering on.
4. Inspect Key Switch
Continuity test key switch in ON position — less than 10 ohms expected. Replace if open.
5. Check Harness Connections
Unplug and reseat all connectors. Visually inspect for corrosion, bent pins, or damage.
6. Controller Voltage
Verify battery voltage (24VDC) reaching controller B+ and B- terminals.
